nodes.text: Back again. Good — the ones who come back are the ones worth teaching. Now, before you buy a single schematic off me, answer me this: where does a bar of bronze *start*?

At the— no. No, no. The furnace is the *middle*. It starts in the ground, same as everything honest in this town. Walk the north spine past Hask's, take the dirt trail east at the lamp — that's the *Amber Delf*. Copper in the west face, tin in the floor. I'm up there at first light most mornings; the town's whole bronze supply is an hour of swinging.

*In the ground.* Ha! There's hope for you. The trail runs east off the north spine, past Hask's — the *Amber Delf*, the old cutting. Copper in the west face, tin in the floor. I'm up there at first light most mornings. An hour of swinging feeds this forge for a day.

So here's your ladder, free of charge: dig copper and tin, smelt bronze at my furnace, hammer it on my spare anvil till your arms understand the work. And when you hit the north face — the gray one that laughs at bronze picks — that's *iron*. Iron wants a better pick, and a better pick wants a better smith. That's not a wall, waker. That's the whole point of walls.

choices.text: I'll go find the Delf first.

nodes.text: Thought you'd never ask. Iron-grade patterns, priced at what they'll earn you back twice over. The paper remembers so your hands don't have to.
Better answer than the schematics, honestly. Off you go — and mind Holloway's cows on the way past. They've opinions about pickaxes.
